title: Streamed audit ingress: compact-index lifecycle & tenant TTL hedging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: With RBAC v2 and expanded SSO/SAML assertions landing in prod, audit volume per tenant is increasing and contains larger payloads (SAML assertions + admin action metadata). Current ingress pipeline appends events to a time-partitioned index and retains full event JSON for 365 days: this is becoming cost-prohibitive and suffers hotspotting for a small set of high-traffic tenants.

Goal: Design and implement a tenant-aware streamed audit ingestion and storage lifecycle that: (1) prevents single-tenant hotspots from blowing up shard capacity, (2) reduces long-term storage costs without losing legal/compliance fidelity for required fields, (3) allows fast recent-window queries (P50/P95 < 300ms for 7d) while providing cold-tier archival for older data, and (4) integrates with RBAC v2 for per-tenant retention policies and SSO-sensitive scrubbing.

Scope: This ticket covers ingestion pre-processing, partitioning strategy, indexing plan, compaction/aggregation options for cold tiers, TTL and archival policies, cost throttles, and a first-pass rollout plan. Separate tickets will cover UI for per-tenant retention controls and billing plumbing.

Design details and decisions: 
- Ingress prefilter & normalization: add a staged preprocessor that: (a) canonicalizes SAML assertion fields to a fixed schema (do NOT store raw full assertions beyond 30 days unless flagged), (b) extracts and indexes three primary keys: tenant_id, subject_id (if present), and action_type, and (c) computes an ingress fingerprint to allow deduping of retries. Prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/3147

- Partitioning: adopt a two-tier partition key: primary = tenant_id_mod(N_hot_shards) for recent hot windows (0–7d), fallback = time-bucket (daily) for cold writes. Hot shards are dynamically sized with a tenant-heap map: tenants that exceed per-tenant qps/size thresholds are assigned dedicated hot-shards to avoid cross-tenant tail latencies. This reduces cross-tenant tail risk and enables tenant-level TTL enforcement.

- Indexing strategy: keep a compact forward index (timestamp, tenant_id, action_type, subject_id, pointer_to_blob) for all events. Full JSON blobs are written to object store (compressed, encrypted) and referenced by pointer. For the first 30 days we keep the blob uncompressed for quicker query paths; after 30d we compress/compact and optionally aggregate repeated events (e.g., heartbeat or health-check events) into summarized counters.

- Compaction & summarization: define configurable compaction policies per action_type. Low-signal high-volume events (metric pings, heartbeats) are downsampled + aggregated by hour after 7 days. High-fidelity admin actions and RBAC changes are never downsampled but may be migrated to coldstore with full retention if compliance requires.

- TTL & tiers: default tenant retention 365d but RBAC-v2 admins can set per-tenant retention to [30, 90, 365, infinite]. Implement TTL hedging: when a tenant reduces retention, mark older segments for expedited compaction but do NOT delete until security review/consent window completes. For tenants with infinite retention, enforce cost controls (billing alerts + quotas).

- Cost controls & backpressure: ingress rate limiter that operates at tenant-level and cluster-level. If estimated daily storage growth for a tenant exceeds quota threshold, we trigger an autoscaling recommendation and apply temporary write-throttles on non-critical events. Metrics exposed in Console: storage_estimate_per_tenant, shard_fill_rate, compaction_lag, cold_migration_rate.

- Security & PII handling: SAML assertions and OIDC tokens are candidate sensitive fields. Implement a pluggable scrubbing pipeline that redacts or tokenizes sensitive keys before persisting full blobs. KMS-integrated encryption for object store. See security doc drafts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Ingress+PII+Handling

- Querying behavior: recent-window queries (0–7d) read directly from hot shards + forward index. Queries older than 7d hit compressed coldstore via a gateway that can expand summaries on-demand. Provide a fallback route for admins to request full blob retrieval for legal requests (audit-runbook link below).

- Monitoring & SLOs: target ingestion availability 99.95%. Query P50/P95 for 7d < 300ms/700ms. Storage cost reduction target: 30% reduction in long-term object-store bytes by applying compaction/shifting-to-cold.

Artifacts and references: 
- Design RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Streamed+Audit+Ingress+RFC
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/3147
- Runbook & incident playbook: https://docs.redwood-infra/runbooks/audit-ingest

Rollout plan (phased): 
1) Canary: route 5% of production traffic (non-PII test tenants) to new preprocessor and hot-shard logic — 2 weeks.
2) Hot-tenant protection: enable tenant-level rate-limits and hot-shard assignment for top 50 tenants — 1 week.
3) Compaction: enable summarization for two low-signal event types and validate storage reduction — 2 weeks.
4) Per-tenant retention controls + UI (PM/design tickets) — parallel.
5) Full migration and opt-in deletion tools once compliance sign-off obtained.

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- How aggressive should default downsampling be? Too aggressive risks losing signal for anomaly detection. Proposed conservative defaults with admin override.
- Do we keep full raw SAML assertions in coldstore for 365d or only 30d? Compliance team prefers 365d; security team recommends 30d plus parsed representation.
- Cost of adding a preprocessor (latency add) vs. saving downstream storage cost. We measured ~8–12ms median overhead in prototype.

Success criteria: 
- No customer-facing incidents for ingress during 5% canary.
- Hotspot CPU/IO tail for shared shards reduced by 60% for top-10 tenants.
- Achieve >=25% long-term storage reduction in first month of compaction.
